diagnosis.statement: The standard local suitable-solution energy identity permits pressure-free local energy increase, decrease and recrossing, while local A+C+D+E remains finite; therefore mere unsigned magnitude bookkeeping and pressure localization do not intrinsically orient temporal local-energy flow.

failure.statement: The inference from finite local A+C+D+E plus the standard local-energy identity and pressure magnitude/localization alone to a universal one-sided local-energy/no-recrossing law is invalid.
failure.scope: Smooth local suitable Navier-Stokes behavior; the exact pressure-free shear is not a global finite-I mild bounded ancient solution and therefore does not falsify a theorem that essentially uses that stronger global/trajectory source class.

gluing_residuals.statement: A local sign counterexample does not decide whether global finite-I mild bounded ancient dynamics imposes an extra no-return law through trajectory, tightness, compactness or minimality information.
No scale-normalized signed observable has yet been defined, shown compact under the Type-I blow-up interface, and connected to a source-valid Liouville/epsilon-regularity consumer.

obstruction.statement: A no-recrossing route cannot obtain orientation merely by re-estimating the same nonnegative local A/C/D/E ledger; it needs an additional signed or genuinely global/trajectory coordinate that survives the finite-I ancient source interface.

lesson.statement: Before pursuing a no-recrossing theorem from a magnitude ledger, ablate candidate sign sources with an exact same-equation solution; if pressure-free or zero-net-convective-flux recrossing survives, introduce an explicit signed/global coordinate rather than another absolute-value estimate.
lesson.falsifier: A source-class theorem deriving one-sidedness solely from the registered unsigned ledger and local identity, with no extra global/trajectory/sign coordinate, would overturn this routing lesson.
